\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{غصہ} (ghussā)}{غصہ (ghussā)}]{\ur{غصہ} (ghussā) — anger}

\label{lesson:UR-C444-ghussa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to fret inwardly, then the Urdu for dejected.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{غصہ}}
\textbf{\ur{غصہ}} — \emph{ghussā} — \textquotedblleft{}anger\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دیر} \ur{سے} \ur{آنے} \ur{پر} \ur{استاد} \ur{کو} \ur{غصہ} \ur{آیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{der se āne par ustād ko ghussā āyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The teacher got angry at someone coming late.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{غصہ}} (\emph{ghussā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ghuṣṣa}, \textquotedblleft{}a choking, a lump in the throat\textquotedblright{}; the sense \textquotedblleft{}anger\textquotedblright{} is the one Urdu gives it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghussā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghussā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{der se āne par ustād ko ghussā āyā.} — The teacher got angry at someone coming late.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to fret inwardly, then the Urdu for dejected, then say \emph{ghussā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{غصہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Anger\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چڑنا} (chiṛnā)}{چڑنا (chiṛnā)}]{\ur{چڑنا} (chiṛnā) — to get irritated}

\label{lesson:UR-C444-chirna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for dejected, then the Urdu for anger.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{چڑنا}} — \emph{chiṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to get irritated\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{ہر} \ur{چھوٹی} \ur{بات} \ur{پر} \ur{چڑتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh har chhoṭī bāt par chiṛtā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He gets irritated over every little thing.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{بچوں} \ur{سے} \ur{چڑی}, \emph{voh bachchoṅ se chiṛī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{چڑنا}} (\emph{chiṛnā}) is inherited from \emph{ciḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}be angry\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 4794).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{برہم} (barham)}{برہم (barham)}]{\ur{برہم} (barham) — incensed; put out}

\label{lesson:UR-C444-barham}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for anger, then the Urdu for to get irritated.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{برہم}}
\textbf{\ur{برہم}} — \emph{barham} — \textquotedblleft{}incensed; put out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{غلط} \ur{بل} \ur{دیکھ} \ur{کر} \ur{گاہک} \ur{برہم} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ghalat bil dekh kar gāhak barham huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The customer was incensed when he saw the wrong bill.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{برہم}} (\emph{barham}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{barham}, \textquotedblleft{}jumbled together, upset\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{طیش} (taish)}{طیش (taish)}]{\ur{طیش} (taish) — a fit of rage}

\label{lesson:UR-C444-taish}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for incensed, then the Urdu for displeased.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{طیش}}
\textbf{\ur{طیش}} — \emph{taish} — \textquotedblleft{}a fit of rage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{طیش} \ur{میں} \ur{آ} \ur{کر} \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{گلاس} \ur{توڑ} \ur{دیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taish meṅ ā kar us ne glās toṛ diyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In a fit of rage he broke the glass.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{طیش}} (\emph{taish}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ṭaysh}, \textquotedblleft{}rashness\textquotedblright{}; the sense \textquotedblleft{}rage\textquotedblright{} is probably a later one.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}
